prompt: Which statement best describes why a wrong product type matters?

options.text: The product type only changes the colour of the order screen.
The product type changes how the position is held, so you must check it before you place an order.
The product type is fixed by Kite and never needs checking.
The product type only matters after the order is filled, never before.

explanations.a: The product type is not a visual setting. It affects how the position is held.
explanations.c: You choose the product type. Kite does not fix it for you.
explanations.d: The product type matters before you place the order. Check it in the order screen.

prompt: You hold shares and set a stop-loss sell with a trigger of Rs 480. The price later falls only to Rs 485. Does the stop trigger?

options.text: Yes. Any fall in price triggers a stop-loss.
No. The price must reach or go below the trigger of Rs 480.
Yes, because a stop-loss always triggers at the day's low.
No. A stop-loss only triggers after the market closes.

explanations.a: A stop-loss needs the price to reach its trigger. A fall to Rs 485 is above Rs 480, so it does not trigger.
explanations.c: The trigger is the price you set. The day's low is not the rule.
explanations.d: A stop-loss can trigger at any time while the market is open. This one does not trigger because the price has not reached Rs 480.

prompt: Spot the mistake: "The product type does not matter, so I can pick any one I like." Which option names the wrong part?

options.text: "The product type does not matter". The product type does matter, because it changes how the position is held.
"Read each product type before you choose". This is correct advice.
"The order type sets the trigger". This is correct for a stop-loss.

explanations.b: This line is correct. Reading the rules of each product type before you choose is the right habit.
explanations.c: This line is correct. For a stop-loss order, the trigger is part of the order type setting.

prompt: Hypothetical. The execution quiz draws 10 questions. How many correct answers are needed to reach 90%?
solution: 90% of 10 = 0.90 x 10 = 9. Check: 9 / 10 = 90%, which passes. 8 / 10 = 80%, which does not.

prompt: Which statement about the demo checklist is correct?

options.text: The book checks your demo results and reports them to Zerodha.
The checklist is self-attested. You tick only what you did.
Each tick sends a report to Zerodha.
Reflections are optional and can stay empty.

explanations.a: The book cannot check your demo. The checklist is self-attested.
explanations.c: No report is sent anywhere. Your results stay on your device.
explanations.d: An empty reflection fails that checklist item.

prompt: One checklist item is ticked, but its reflection box is empty. What happens to that item?

options.text: It passes, because the tick is enough.
It fails, because an empty reflection fails the item.
Only the quiz is checked, so the item is ignored.
It passes after one retake of the quiz.

explanations.a: The tick alone is not enough. The reflection must have words in it.
explanations.c: Every checklist item is checked, and the quiz does not replace an item.
explanations.d: A quiz retake does not change an empty reflection. Write the reflection to pass that item.
